sampling_model.design: Superpopulation observational sampling with no parametric model for the categorical distribution, propensities, or outcome regressions.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment \(A\) with identification by consistency and conditional exchangeability given \(X\).
sampling_model.overlap: Fixed \(\epsilon\le P(A=1\mid X=k)\le1-\epsilon\) on every positive-mass category.
sampling_model.outcome: Real outcomes with \(|\mu_{ak}|\le M\) and explicitly imposed unstandardized conditional fourth central moments at most \(M^4\); this implies conditional variances at most \(M^2\) but imposes no standardized-kurtosis or positive-variance condition.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On the balanced local class, the explicit cross-fitted saturated-cell nuisance estimators have derived weighted squared-error order \(d_n/n\), which yields the one-step orthogonal remainder \(O_P(d_n/n)\). The heavy-light handle uses the pilot rule \(\min_aN_{ak}^{(0)}\le256\log(en)\) and exactly equals the saturated one-step center and variance when every category is heavy; its radii remain proposed outputs.
sampling_model.computation: Categorical and treatment coordinates are exact and outcomes have dyadic enclosures. Polynomial and falling-factorial recurrences admit outward interval evaluation, but certified bisection is unavailable until the nonmonotone light score is replaced or confined to a bracket with a uniform positive slope and the heavy score is explicitly specified.
sampling_model.randomness: All probabilities and expectations are under the observed iid sample law \(Q_P^{(n)}=P_O^{\otimes n}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 on pages 8--10 lower-bounds worst-case mean squared error for the one-arm functional \(\psi_1\) by the order of \(n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2 n]\) under fixed overlap; Appendix C.5 sets the control-arm regression to zero in the hard family.
The paper constructs heavy-light best-polynomial factorial-moment estimators attaining minimax mean squared error for additive discrete-distribution functionals.

Sections 4.1--4.2 provide scalar bounded-influence score inequalities, but they do not prove a tail theorem for this pilot-selected marked-factorial statistic; moreover, the symmetric half-log transform stipulated here is not globally monotone and needs a retained-range theorem or score replacement before root inversion is valid.
Theorem 1 lower-bounds expected confidence length in Gaussian nonparametric experiments by a between-class modulus and the paper constructs constant-factor adaptive intervals.
Theorem 5.1 gives uniformly valid asymptotically efficient Gaussian ATE intervals from cross-fitted orthogonal scores under nuisance-rate conditions.

The Abstract and Sections 2--4 derive finite-sample optimal bias-aware ATE estimators and confidence intervals under smoothness or shape restrictions when regression errors are normal with known variance, with feasible asymptotic extensions for unknown errors.

Theorem 3.1 gives a self-normalized moderate-deviation expansion for fixed-order nondegenerate Studentized U-statistics under moment conditions; its degree-one consequence is used only for the oracle-score central limit step.
The paper gives nearly tight dimension-free confidence intervals for probabilities of individually unobserved multinomial events.

body.tldr: The same-class testing converse is established, and the strongest unconditional honest-length result is currently the bracket \(r_{n,d,M}\lesssim_{\epsilon,\alpha}\mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}\le4M\). This round separately proves the saturated one-step expansion, ratio-consistent variance, and Gaussian limit, proves that every pilot arm-cell is heavy with probability \(1-o(1)\) on the balanced local class, and corrects the heavy-light handle to impose the exact all-heavy center/variance override. The sharp global upper bound, certified computation, heavy-light radius limit, and endpoint equivalence remain open because neither the selected-factorial radius nor the hybrid heavy Gaussian/fallback radius is defined and certified.

project_justification.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 supplies the large-alphabet point-risk obstruction and the \(n=9915,d=8196\) 401(k) application, but not a directly calibrated honest expected-length upper bound. The accepted factorial construction supplies the light approximation bias, while the stipulated symmetric half-log score is nonmonotone and the heavy Gaussian/fallback score is absent.
project_justification.niche: The unresolved contribution is a globally honest interval for arbitrary categorical masses that also uses the efficient Gaussian radius on balanced tables. The exact all-heavy override now makes this adaptive target mathematically well posed without treating the local one-step benchmark as a substitute for it.
project_justification.fill: The core now contains a proved same-class lower bound, a closed fallback bracket, a proved saturated one-step local benchmark, and an exponential all-heavy pilot bound. Completion requires an explicit monotone selected-factorial calibration with pilot-shift control and an explicit heavy score whose high-variance branch has Gaussian critical value and whose fallback branch is finite-sample honest.

body.related_work: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 remains the application and point-risk anchor and supports the moment-matching architecture behind the proved same-class converse, but it does not supply the present honest upper interval. CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026 supplies the clipped real-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator and light-bias architecture, not a direct tail theorem. Catoni2012 provides scalar bounded-influence inequalities but not unique-root calibration for the redescending symmetric half-log score used here. ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML and Hahn1998 are matched by the separate proved saturated one-step benchmark; they do not connect that benchmark to a finite-sample honest arbitrary-mass interval. ShaoZhou2016 supports only the already-declared degree-one self-normalized central-limit step. ArmstrongKolesar2021, CaiLow2004, and Painsky2022 remain adjacent comparators rather than sources of the missing global construction.
body.technical_internal_limitation: For the stipulated symmetric score, \(\psi'(x)=2(2-x^2)/(x^4+4)\), so the score is redescending, has stationary points at \(\pm\sqrt2\), and can have at least three roots. Thus monotone inversion and a uniform score-to-root error modulus are unavailable. Conditioning on the common pilot also centers block fluctuations at a pilot-dependent mean rather than the unconditional expectation. Separately, no heavy hybrid score presently combines a studentized Gaussian branch with a bounded-influence finite-sample fallback.
body.honest_scope: The global model still permits arbitrary and zero cell masses and imposes only fixed overlap, bounded cell means, and an absolute conditional fourth-central-moment envelope. No standardized-kurtosis, positive conditional-variance, or global balance condition is added. The established confidence-length conclusion is the lower bound together with the deterministic \([-2M,2M]\) upper bracket. The balanced mass and nondegenerate efficient-variance conditions are used only for the proved one-step benchmark and all-heavy probability lemma; finite-sample heavy-light coverage, sharp expected length, certified endpoints, and heavy-light Gaussian endpoint equivalence remain open.
body.interpretation: When cell masses are balanced and \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\), every pilot arm-cell exceeds the heavy threshold with probability \(1-o(1)\), and the corrected heavy-light center and variance then equal the efficient saturated one-step outputs. This proves that the center can adapt locally. It does not yet justify Gaussian heavy-light endpoints: that conclusion additionally requires the unresolved hybrid radius to approach \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)/n}\).
